title: Unique Length-3 Palindromic Subsequences
spaceBreakdown:
- int first[26], last[26]: fixed 26 ints → O(1)
- bool seen[26]: fixed 26 bools → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input string s, returned int
approach: A length-3 palindrome has the form "xyx": the same outer character x on both ends and any middle character y. For each of the 26 letters x, find its first and last occurrence in s; if they differ, every distinct letter appearing strictly between them can serve as y, each yielding a unique "xyx". Summing these distinct-middle counts over all x gives the answer. This is correct because using the earliest first and latest last occurrence of x maximizes the middle window, so any valid y for any pair of x-occurrences is captured, and distinct middle letters produce distinct 3-letter strings.
hints: A length-3 palindrome is always of the form "xyx". For a fixed outer character x that appears several times in s, which two of its occurrences would leave the most room for middle characters y between them? (n ≤ 10^5 rules out checking every triplet.)
For each of the 26 letters, store its first and last index in s. In "aabca", 'a' has first=0 and last=4; any letter appearing in s[1..3] ("abc") forms a valid "aya" palindrome, contributing 3.

```
for each letter c in 'a'..'z':
    first[c] = first index of c in s
    last[c]  = last index of c in s
    if first[c] < last[c]:
        mark every distinct letter in s[first[c]+1 .. last[c]-1]
        add the count of marked letters to answer
return answer
```

**All same characters** - every position holds the same letter
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: counting each index triple (i,j,k) with i<j<k and s[i]==s[k] without deduplicating the resulting string → returns 4

**Off-by-one on the right endpoint** - minimal valid palindrome
`Input: s = "aba"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: counting distinct letters in s[first+1 .. last] inclusive of the last endpoint → returns 2 (falsely counts 'a' as a middle char, yielding "aaa" which needs 3 a's)

**Outer char appears twice with no room** - adjacent equal letters
`Input: s = "aab"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: iterating the middle range as s[first+1 .. last] inclusive (right off-by-one) → returns 1 (counts 'a' at index 1 as middle, but "aaa" is not a subsequence of "aab")

**Multiple outer characters** - several letters each appear at both ends
`Input: s = "abacaba"` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: not resetting the "seen middle letters" set between different outer characters → returns 6 (accumulates {a,b,c} from 'a' and reuses it for 'b')

followUps.q: What if the palindrome length is 5 (form "xyzyx") instead of 3?
followUps.a: For each ordered pair of outer characters (x, z), find the first x and last x, then within that window find the first z and last z, and count distinct middle characters y between them. Time becomes O(|Σ|² · n) = O(26² · n), space stays O(|Σ|). It generalizes to length L as O(|Σ|^(L/2) · n).

followUps.q: What if the alphabet includes uppercase letters and digits (|Σ| = 62)?
followUps.a: Replace the size-26 arrays with size-62 (or 128) arrays; the algorithm is unchanged. Time becomes O(62 · n), space O(62). For an unbounded alphabet (Unicode), use hash maps for first/last and a hash set for middle characters, giving O(n · |distinct chars|) time.

followUps.q: What if you must answer many queries counting unique length-3 palindromic subsequences on arbitrary substrings s[l..r]?
followUps.a: Precompute per-character sorted position lists and a prefix bitmask of letters seen up to each index. For a query, for each letter c binary-search its first and last occurrence within [l..r], then use prefix bitmasks to count distinct letters strictly between them in O(1). Preprocessing O(n), each query O(|Σ| · log n), space O(n + |Σ|).
